The point of this Theater production is the rare opportunity to see a pivotal American period piece staged deeply into the period by Bartlett Sher ("South Pacific") with a huge, expert cast that only a nonprofit can afford to showcase with such luxurious dedication today on Broadway.

A dazzling revival of Clifford Odets' 'Golden Boy' opened Thursday, still packing a punch after 75 years.
There’s no easy solution in “Golden Boy,” and the play hurtles forward with the momentum of tragedy.
You'll be hard-pressed to find a production, even in this season of robust revivals, that packs more visceral punch.
That aside, this Depression-era, 1937 revival is riveting for just about every moment of the nearly 3 hours, two intermissions at the Belasco Theatre, where Golden Boy first appeared.
"Golden Boy" is grand and glorious theater.
How lucky we are to have Theater bring back Clifford Odets' rarely seen 1937 boxing tragedy 'Golden Boy' in an altogether gripping revival.

cn.t: Odets' 75-year-old boxing drama still packs a punch in Bartlett Sher's robust revival, with critics praising the excellent ensemble cast led by Numrich and Shalhoub, though some find the melodrama creaky and pacing uneven.
